titolo: How Knight Capital Lost $440,000,000 in 45 Minutes

copertina.immagine: A glowing red button on a dark trading desk, golden coins melting and pouring off the edge into darkness

shots.voce: In forty-five minutes, one of Wall Street's biggest traders lost four hundred forty million dollars. No hack. No fraud. Just one forgotten piece of old code.
shots.immagine: A giant stack of golden coins collapsing and dissolving into red sparks inside a dark vault

shots.voce: August first, twenty twelve. Knight Capital was a market maker, handling billions of dollars in stock trades every single day, and it had just upgraded its trading software.
shots.immagine: A sleek glass trading floor with rows of faceless 3D figures at glowing blue screens showing abstract charts

shots.voce: Technicians had installed the new software on seven of eight servers. On the eighth, the old code stayed behind, and nobody noticed the mistake.
shots.immagine: A row of eight server racks, seven glowing blue and one dim, flickering amber at the end

shots.voce: At nine thirty a.m., the market opened. The new system's trigger woke the old code on that eighth server, a dormant function from years before.
shots.immagine: A giant analog clock striking nine thirty as a single server door swings open releasing red light

shots.voce: The old code began firing orders nonstop, buying and selling stocks at a furious pace. Within minutes, prices of dozens of stocks started jumping strangely.
shots.immagine: A wall of trading screens without readable text, spiking red lines multiplying across every display

shots.voce: Inside Knight, engineers scrambled to find the cause. The machine kept trading millions of shares, losing money on almost every single order it sent.
shots.immagine: Faceless 3D figures running between desks in a bright office as streams of golden coins pour out of a server

shots.voce: Someone rolled back the new software, which made things worse. The old code now ran on every server, and the losses grew faster.
shots.immagine: A glowing red button being pressed by a faceless figure, red cracks spreading across eight server racks

shots.voce: At ten fifteen, the trading finally stopped. Knight was left holding positions worth billions, and its loss stood at about four hundred forty million dollars.
shots.immagine: A clock reading ten fifteen above a heap of dull, tarnished coins in a silent, darkened trading room

shots.voce: Knight's whole profit for a year was far smaller than that loss. Within months, the company needed a rescue and was soon sold. Subscribe to see how the next one happened.
shots.immagine: An empty office at dusk, one dark monitor and a single fallen golden coin on the floor
